newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Proposed highway seeks to compete with Panama Canal.
newsitem.headline: Proposed highway seeks to compete with Panama Canal.

text.p: Investors from Honduras and El Salvador said on Wednesday they planned to build a highway linking the Pacific and Atlantic oceans across the Central American isthmus in a bid to compete with the Panama Canal.

Miguel Facusse, one of Honduras' top business leaders, said the plan would be part of the proposed $18 billion Great National Transformation Project announced by private investors last year that seeks to bolster Honduran infrastructure.
He offered no cost for the canal project, which he said could begin as soon as next February with work on Pacific and Atlantic ports as well as the highway.
"This highway will offer an alternative to international trade," Facusse said during a luncheon meeting with President Carlos Roberto Reina.

The proposed project would link Pacific and Atlantic ports with a highway so containers of goods could be unloaded on one coast, driven across the isthmus, and unloaded on another boat on the other side.
It is similar to a proposal by an international consortium that hopes to build a so-called "dry canal" in neighboring Nicaragua, but the Nicaraguan proposal would do the same with a high-speed rail.
"This will permit us to integrate our internal markets and centralize in Honduras the economic integration of Central America," he said.
